letter_text: I sit by the window often these days. I look outside, then inside, then outside again, and time just goes by. If someone calls my name, I answer. If no one calls, I just stay there. I'm not sure if this is laziness or rest. How is it for you?

Last week I heard that an old friend had died. I didn't go to the funeral. It seemed like the right thing to do, but my body wouldn't move. I'm not sad even now. That is what feels stranger. I don't know what's normal anymore.

When I'm in a crowded place, I find a corner. I'm not doing it on purpose, but somehow I end up standing there. If someone speaks to me, I answer briefly. I could say more, but I cut it short. Sometimes I envy the ones who keep talking.

Some days just pass through me. I can't really remember what happened. I look at photos and I must have been there, but the feeling of that day doesn't come back. If someone brings it up, I just say 'oh, right, that.' It's all gone.
I'm fine. Really, I'm fine. People keep saying I don't look fine, and that's starting to bother me. I know my own state best. I'm just tired. A few nights of sleep and it'll pass.

In some moments, I feel like I'm not there. My body is, but my mind is somewhere else. I was in a meeting once, and when it ended I couldn't remember what was said. Everyone told me I was listening well. I don't know if that's frightening or comforting.

I have to finish the work first. I'll deal with the feelings later, I tell myself, but 'later' doesn't come. Late at night, when I'm alone, something rises for a moment, and then I sleep. By morning there's another task. Maybe this is what becoming an adult means.

We broke up. I thought about why for several days. Our patterns, attachment styles, our childhoods — I have it all sorted out. When it's sorted out, I get calmer. A friend asked, 'so are you sad?' I said, 'I'm not sure about that part yet.'

Lately, the way other people get excited feels far away to me. I can't quite follow what they're so happy or angry about. I'm with them, but it doesn't feel like I'm with them. I'm not sure if I changed or they did.

The test results came back. They aren't good. The doctor explained things calmly, and I listened calmly. I took notes. I came home and explained the same way to my family. They cried. I didn't. A few days later, in the bathroom, I cried for a moment. Once.

author_pseudonym: the one with the radio on
letter_text: I leave the radio on while I cook, while I drive, before I sleep. Silence is when something almost-shaped tries to come up. I don't know what it is. I don't want to find out tonight either. Maybe one day I'll let the room be quiet.

author_pseudonym: the one with the lights on
letter_text: I leave every light in the house on. I sleep better that way. People keep asking if something happened and I say no, I just like the brightness. They don't believe me. I'm not sure what to do with that disbelief, so I turn another lamp on.

I drove home from work yesterday and I don't remember any of it. The car is in the driveway. The keys are on the counter. That hour of the afternoon is just missing. It happens more often than I'd like to admit. I haven't told anyone.

author_pseudonym: the one with the short fuse
blank_answer: say things before I know I mean them
letter_text: I open my mouth and the words are already out. By the time I hear them, it's too late. The other person flinches, and I flinch too, on the inside. I tell myself I'll wait next time. Sometimes I do. Most times the fuse is lit before I notice it.

blank_answer: heat that carries from the morning into the afternoon
letter_text: I had a hard call before lunch and was sharp with the cashier by two. I knew while I was doing it. I couldn't stop in time. I went back to the same store the next day and bought something small from her. She was kind about it. I don't think she remembered.

blank_answer: would rather not carry it alone
letter_text: When I find out something hard, I want to tell someone within the hour. I used to think this was weakness. Now I think it's how I metabolize. The thing gets smaller as soon as it's in another person's ear. Maybe that's not maturity, but it keeps me upright.

blank_answer: shows up when someone is sick
letter_text: I drove four hours last weekend to sit with a friend after her surgery. I made soup, walked her dog, didn't talk much. I came home tired and clearer than I'd been in months. I'm not sure if that's generosity or something else, but it's the realest I've felt all year.

author_pseudonym: the one with the bag packed
blank_answer: a small bag, in case the news is bad
letter_text: I keep a small bag packed by the door this winter — a change of clothes, a phone charger, the names of the medications. My mother is older than she's ever been. The bag isn't fear exactly. It's more like making the future a little softer for the version of me who'll need it.

author_pseudonym: the one in the small house
blank_answer: imagine the small house in my head
letter_text: I keep returning to a small house with a field beyond the window. No neighbors. A kettle. A chair. No one knows the address. I don't think I want to live there. I want to know it exists. On hard days I sit in it for an hour and the day softens.

blank_answer: the world I made up is kinder
letter_text: When the day gets too loud I drift into a version of it I made up, where the people are kinder and the rooms are quieter. I don't tell anyone I'm doing this. I come back when called. I'm starting to wonder how much time I've spent in there.

I left another second date behind last week. By dessert I'd already started cataloging the small ways he wasn't quite right. He was kind. He called the next day. I didn't answer. I'm starting to wonder if I'm protecting myself from something or just from people.

blank_answer: an anger I can't quite address
letter_text: I carry an anger I can't properly direct. The person who hurt me is two states away and won't answer. So the kettle gets it. The cabinet gets it. The dog watches from the rug. Most days now I can put it down before I open the door. Most.

blank_answer: the same complaint, a little altered
letter_text: I keep going back to the same story with my friend. She's tried every angle. I've found a flaw in every angle. She's stopped suggesting things. I miss the suggestions. I think I'd like to let one of them work this week, even imperfectly, and see what happens.

author_pseudonym: the one who laughs in waiting rooms
letter_text: I laughed quietly in the waiting room before my mother's surgery. Not because anything was funny, exactly — because the alternative was a kind of stiffness I couldn't survive in for two more hours. The nurse smiled. So did my mother, when I told her later. We needed it.

author_pseudonym: the one with the imagined mother
blank_answer: the version of her who would have understood
letter_text: I keep going back to the mother I made up — the one who would have understood, who would have asked the right question, who would have stayed in the room. The real one is more complicated. The imagined one is more comforting. I'm slowly learning to let both exist in the same week.

author_pseudonym: the one with the long list
blank_answer: a long list of what I owe people
letter_text: I carry a list of what I owe people, or what I think I owe them. Calls to return, favors to repay, meals to make. The list never ends. I'm not sure I asked for half of these debts. I'm trying, this month, to take one off without paying it, just to see if the world holds.

author_pseudonym: the one with the unsent draft
blank_answer: a sentence in a draft email from last spring
letter_text: I left a sentence unsent in a draft from last spring — the thing I couldn't say to my manager. Instead I forwarded the work slightly late, with a polite note. He noticed. He didn't say anything. I noticed he noticed. That whole quiet exchange did more damage than the sentence would have.

blank_answer: the feeling that I'm being judged
letter_text: I keep going back to the feeling that I'm being judged. I walk into rooms with that weight already there. Last week a friend told me she'd been thinking, the whole dinner, that I seemed warm. I almost didn't believe her. I'm starting to suspect the judging voice is mostly mine.

blank_answer: is sure people are not on her side
letter_text: I'm sure my new neighbor doesn't like me. I have evidence — the way she nodded, the small pause, the closed window. None of it is evidence, really. I'm slowly learning that what I'm reading on her face is sometimes a sentence I wrote and forgot to sign.

author_pseudonym: the calm one others get edgy around
blank_answer: stays calm while the room gets edgy
letter_text: I'm calm, sometimes too calm, and the people with me start fidgeting and raising their voices. Afterwards I tell myself I had nothing to do with it. I'm not sure that's true anymore. Some of what I'm not feeling seems to land in whoever's nearest. I'd like to start carrying my share.

blank_answer: the smoother version of the story
letter_text: I keep going back to the smoother explanation I gave myself because it lets me sleep. The rougher version surfaces sometimes — usually around 3 a.m. — and I usually push it back under. Lately I've been letting it sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before I do.

blank_answer: tell everyone how happy I am for them
letter_text: When my friend's career took off last year, I told everyone how thrilled I was. The volume of my happiness was louder than the feeling could carry. I think I knew. Now, quieter, I can also be a little jealous and still glad for her. The two fit in the same week, it turns out.

blank_answer: is harder to talk over now
letter_text: I used to lose the end of my sentences in meetings. Now, more often than not, I finish them. It isn't comfortable. People are surprised. So am I. The difference it makes — in what gets decided, in how I feel walking home — is bigger than I expected.

blank_answer: the small things I do under pressure
letter_text: Under pressure my voice goes higher, I avoid certain calls, I reach for sugar at midnight. I used to be embarrassed by these patterns. Now I read them like a mirror, plainly. Knowing them makes them smaller. Knowing them earlier makes them smaller still.

After one hard night, my steady partner becomes someone I never really knew. By morning he is back to being the man who makes my coffee. I don't tell him about the rewriting; I'm not proud of it. The ones who can wait through that storm get to stay. He's been patient. I'm grateful, quietly.

blank_answer: the garden after a hard week
letter_text: I keep going back to the garden after a hard week. Whatever didn't get said in the meeting goes into the soil. By the end of an afternoon I'm tired in my body and quiet in my head, and the tomatoes don't know any of it. I keep thinking that's a good arrangement.

blank_answer: check every light I turned off, twice
letter_text: I went back to the kitchen three times tonight to make sure the stove was off. Each time it was. The checking isn't really about the stove. It's a small ritual that keeps something else at bay — I'm not sure what yet. I'm trying to ask the question instead of doing the loop.

author_pseudonym: the one who locks the drawer
letter_text: There is a drawer in my chest I keep closed. I know what is in it. I open it on Sundays for a moment, then close it again. People say I should write it down, but writing it would mean carrying it during the week, and the week is already long. I think you understand. I'll keep the drawer closed until next Sunday.

I have a small box under my desk. Every time something hard happens I put it in the box and shut the lid. I tell myself I will open it on a quieter night. The box is full now. The night never gets quiet. I am still putting things in. Are you also waiting for a quieter night?

When my father called me last week, I wrote down what we said on a yellow pad. Afterward I underlined the parts that might matter and drew arrows between them. I have not looked at the pad since. The arrows tell me where the feeling is supposed to be. I am still finding the room with the feeling in it.

author_pseudonym: the one who reads about it
letter_text: After my friend died I bought four books about grief. I underlined them. I can tell you the stages and the order. I cannot tell you what color her kitchen was. I keep underlining. I think I am writing a map around a country I will not enter. You don't have to enter it either. Just sit with me at the border.

author_pseudonym: the one at the kitchen table
blank_answer: someone is in the kitchen with me
letter_text: Today was a hard day, so I called my sister and asked her to stay on the line while I washed dishes. We didn't talk much. She did the crossword. Hearing her pen on the paper through the phone was enough. I think this is what people mean by leaning. I leaned. The dishes are done.

author_pseudonym: the one with the long thread
letter_text: There is a group chat from eleven years ago that still beeps almost every day. Most of what we say is nothing. Someone shares a song. Someone says they're at the dentist. I read every message. When I am most alone I scroll back to the beginning and read forward until I'm tired. We are still here, all of us. Are you somewhere reading too?

I had a heavy week, so on Saturday I cooked too much rice and brought a bowl to my neighbor. She is older and forgets to eat. We sat at her small table without speaking much. Watching her eat made my own week feel lighter, which embarrasses me a little. I do not know if that is honest care or if I'm using her. Maybe both can be true. I'll bring rice again next week.

A friend has been calling me late at night. She talks for an hour. I listen. After we hang up I notice I feel calmer, even when I had been crying earlier. I do not tell her that. It would be strange to thank her for letting me listen. I am writing it down here instead. Thank you, somebody, for letting me listen.

author_pseudonym: the one with a small bag
blank_answer: a packed bag by the door
letter_text: I have a small bag by the door with a phone charger, a sweater, my passport. Nothing is happening. I just like knowing the bag is there. My partner thinks it's strange. I think it means I can imagine the next thing without it crushing me. I am not running from anything. I am just less afraid because the bag is packed. Do you have a bag like that?

There is a conversation I have to have on Tuesday. I have already had it in my head four times. Each time I imagine it going a little worse so the real version cannot surprise me. This is not catastrophizing. It is a small homework. By Tuesday I think I will be tired but ready. If it goes badly I will already have a script for the next morning. That counts as kindness to myself, I think.

author_pseudonym: the one who calls it nothing
letter_text: I didn't get the job. Honestly, the company was bad anyway. The manager looked tired in the interview. The office had ugly chairs. I would not have stayed long. I tell my friends this and they laugh, but I notice my chest is still tight. Maybe I am protecting something soft by making the lost thing small. I'll let you decide.

blank_answer: make it smaller in my head
letter_text: She stopped texting me back three weeks ago. I keep telling myself she was never that close. We only met a few times. The trip we planned was probably going to fall through anyway. The more I say this the smaller she gets in my head, until I almost cannot remember why I once liked her. I am writing this so I remember that I did.

author_pseudonym: the one who slams the cupboard
letter_text: I yelled at my partner today because the rice cooker beeped wrong. The rice cooker was not the problem. My boss had said something at noon that I could not say anything back to. By dinner the boss was nowhere and the rice cooker was right there. I'm sorry, rice cooker. I'm sorry, partner. I will try to say the boss's name out loud next time, even alone in the car.

author_pseudonym: the one with the heavy bag
letter_text: After a fight with my mother I went to the gym. I hit the heavy bag for forty minutes. I am not a person who hits things. I sat on the floor afterward and my hands were shaking. The bag took what I could not give back to her. I do not know if that's healing or just rearranging. I left the gym lights on for the next person.

author_pseudonym: the one who waves them off
letter_text: Everyone keeps offering me advice. Try therapy. Try a walk. Try writing it down. Each one feels like a small door closing. I say 'I've tried that' before they finish. Maybe I am not asking for solutions. Maybe I am asking someone to stand near me in the unfixed part. I don't know how to say that, so I keep complaining. I hope someone hears the real request underneath.

author_pseudonym: the one with the unsolvable thing
letter_text: When my friend asks how I am, I list the things I've already tried that did not work. She gets a little tired. I get a little safer. As long as nothing has worked, no one can take the problem from me, and the problem is the part I know best. I don't want to scare it away. Today I want to try, just once, to say 'I'm tired' without the list. I'll let you know how it goes.

author_pseudonym: the one who tells a joke at the funeral
blank_answer: make a joke at the wrong moment
letter_text: At my grandfather's funeral I told a joke about his terrible driving. People laughed. Then I cried. Then I laughed again. The joke was true and it was tender, and I could not have said the tender part without the joke first. I am not making light. I am building a small staircase down into the heavy place. Step, step.

author_pseudonym: the one who laughs at the doctor
letter_text: I made the nurse laugh today. The test results were not good. I cracked a joke about the gown opening in the back and she laughed and the doctor laughed and for a minute the room was a different room. Later, in the parking lot, I sat in the car and did not laugh. Both rooms were real. I am writing from the parking lot.

author_pseudonym: the one who keeps the letter
blank_answer: the version of her I loved
letter_text: I keep one letter from my mother in a drawer. In it she is patient and clear and on my side. She wrote it in 1998. She has not been that person for a long time. I read the letter twice a year. I know I am loving a version that no longer lives in her, and maybe never fully did. I love the version anyway. It keeps me kinder to the woman who actually answers the phone now.

Whenever I describe my old teacher to friends, he becomes better and better. By the third telling he is a saint. I know he had a temper. I know he forgot my name once for a whole semester. I do this because I needed someone to be that good when I was sixteen, and the polished version still does that work. I am only slowly letting him be a person again.

author_pseudonym: the one who holds it all
letter_text: When my sister called crying I said, 'I'll handle it.' I always say that. By the end of the week I had called her landlord, fixed her resume, lent her money, and not slept. I felt enormous and useful and also slightly sick. I think part of me was afraid that if I let her handle even one thing, she would not need me at all. I am trying to give her back one small task this week. Just one.

I keep everyone's schedules in my head. My mother's doctor appointments. My partner's deadlines. My friend's medication times. People say it's impressive. It is also how I make sure no one leaves. If I am the one who remembers, I am the one who is needed. I am trying to write things on paper instead of holding them in my chest. Paper is heavy too, but not in the same way.

author_pseudonym: the one with the late reply
letter_text: She asked a favor of me on Monday. I knew immediately that I did not want to do it. I could not say no, so I waited four days to reply. By then it was almost too late to help, which was the point. I felt clever and small at the same time. I am writing this to admit that 'too busy' was not the real answer. The real answer was 'I am tired of being the one you ask.'

author_pseudonym: the one who forgets on purpose
letter_text: My partner asked me twice to pick up bread on the way home. I did not pick up bread. I told myself I forgot. I did not forget. I was angry about something else and I did not have words for it, so the bread became the message. I am trying to find the words. They are slow in coming. Until then, I owe somebody a loaf.

author_pseudonym: the one who makes them angry
blank_answer: wait for them to be the angry one
letter_text: When I am angry I get very quiet. I say small careful things. Within an hour the other person is shouting and I am calm. They become the angry one and I become the patient one. It works every time. I know it is not honest. The anger does not leave me. It just rents a different body for the evening. I am trying to keep it in my own chest, even when it's loud there.

blank_answer: explain why it was for the best
letter_text: I quit the band last year. I tell people I needed time to focus on my career, which is true. I also tell them the singer was difficult, which is true. I do not tell them I was scared to perform. That is also true. The first two reasons are good reasons. The third is the real reason. I keep the third in my pocket. I am taking it out a little today, just for you.

There is a coworker I cannot stand. When I see her I smile wider than I smile at anyone else. I send her thoughtful messages on her birthday. I bring her coffee. The kinder I am to her, the louder the other thing gets in private. I am tired. I do not want to wish her well anymore, and I do not want to wish her ill. I want to be allowed to feel something in the middle. I am practicing.

author_pseudonym: the one who said no on Tuesday
letter_text: On Tuesday I told my boss I could not take on the new project. I did not apologize. I did not add 'sorry' or 'maybe later' or 'if you really need me.' I just said no, and then I let the room be quiet. My hands were shaking under the table. He nodded and we moved on. That sentence used three seconds. I have been recovering for two days. It was worth it.

On the bus home I caught myself watching myself be tired. I noticed I was clenching my jaw. I noticed I was annoyed at a stranger for no reason. I noticed I noticed. It was a quiet kind of company. Nothing changed about the day. But I was, for a moment, two people instead of one, and the second one was patient with the first. I'll try to find her again tomorrow.

After the fight with my brother I sat at the piano for an hour. I was not playing songs. I was just pressing the same three notes in different orders. By the end my chest was looser. I had not solved anything with him. But the thing inside me had been given somewhere to go that wasn't his face. The piano did not mind. I think this is what people mean by music. I am writing to you instead of playing tonight.
